conclusion.justification: The report highlights both positive meta-analyses and high-quality conflicting evidence (such as the 2020 Cochrane review and large NEJM trials), concluding that current evidence is mixed, inconsistent, and uncertain. Therefore, it treats the evidence as balanced/insufficient without making a definitive directional claim.

report:
# Do Probiotics Shorten Acute Infectious Diarrhea? The Evidence Is Mixed

Your assumption that the answer is "yes" reflects the older consensus, but the most recent high-quality evidence has shifted toward uncertainty.

## Earlier Evidence Supporting Benefit

The 2010 Cochrane review concluded that probiotics, used alongside rehydration therapy, had "clear beneficial effects in shortening the duration and reducing stool frequency in acute infectious diarrhoea" (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6532699/). Multiple meta-analyses have echoed this, with one citing an approximately 25-hour reduction in diarrhea duration (https://www.medicalnewstoday.com/articles/probiotics-for-diarrhea). A 2025 meta-analysis of 19 RCTs in children also found probiotics shortened diarrhea duration (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pediatrics/articles/10.3389/fped.2025.1722257/full).

## Updated High-Quality Evidence Casting Doubt

The **updated 2020 Cochrane review** reversed the earlier conclusion, stating: "Probiotics may not affect how long acute diarrhoea lasts. We do not know if they can shorten the time to recovery" and "probably make little or no difference to the number of people who have diarrhoea lasting 48 hours or longer" (https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD003048.pub4/full).

Two large **NEJM randomized trials (2018)** in nearly 1,900 children with acute gastroenteritis found **no benefit** from *L. rhamnosus* GG or a combination probiotic on diarrhea duration, frequency, or other outcomes (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1802598).

## Conclusion

The answer is **not a straightforward yes**. While many meta-analyses suggest probiotics modestly shorten diarrhea duration, the most recent Cochrane review and two large, well-designed NEJM trials found little or no benefit. Current evidence is inconsistent and may depend on strain, population, and setting.
